headline: Today is the publish day for the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short and the last day for Tipu Sultan, whose English readership rose to 2.64x its usual as the row reached street protests in Latur. Neither has a script on disk. The Sonia Gandhi Short failed its day-three test, so recent-politics Shorts come off the list.

top3.signal: Tomorrow, the top date in the calendar; the searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. No script is on disk.
top3.recommendation: Publish today at 17:00 IST, titled with his name first. Judge it on its search views over the year, not on its third day.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan: the row moved to the street
top3.signal: English Wikipedia readership at 2.64x its 30-day median, 2,980 a day over three days, up from yesterday. On 22 November BJP workers protested in Latur against Congress MLA Amit Deshmukh's Tipu remarks (Mid-Day, ThePrint); on 21 November The Hindu reported his descendant's call for official celebrations.
top3.recommendation: Publish tonight after Tegh Bahadur as “Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It”, or press Drop. The decision lapses tomorrow either way.

top3.signal: Seven days out, and the recording step falls today. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level, so this rests on the date alone.
top3.recommendation: Next onto the list when Tipu's place frees tomorrow: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943 convicted from British papers (War Cabinet minutes, Leo Amery's diary), published 30 November. The channel's earlier Churchill Short lost its viewers to a context dump; its lesson: “The one-sentence context rule applies inside the first 10 seconds most of all.”

more.signal: 11 days out; the research step is due now. The channel's earlier Short, “How Missionaries Turned Sati Into a Fundraiser”, brought one subscriber, and a commenter there gave the sharper angle: the people who burned witches in Europe stopped sati in India.
more.recommendation: Watch, not yet a decision. Check whether the wife-selling script on disk (written 17 September, not recorded) is still unpublished; if so it fits this date on the same hypocrisy. Every claim checked before recording.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form this week: long-form views rose 18.0% week over week, and the video has 90,680 views in 5 days. New long-forms have brought 555 subscribers this month against 105 planned, and over 28 days long-form earns 83.3% of upload net subscribers.

The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views: a villain convicted by his own record, then the people still repeating his version. That is the Tipu Short's shape: who took the treasure, then who wrote the story.
The British officers' pay Short (22 November) is liked by 8.5% of its viewers against a Shorts median of 3.9%. It is on its first day, so judge it on 25 November.
whats_wrong: Neither dated Short has a script on disk, and the slot went to the owner's own pick again. Probable cause: the owner's own scripts are the ones that get recorded. Test: none, it is a choice; today it has to be Tegh Bahadur, because the date will not move.

The Sonia Gandhi Short failed its day-three test: 912 views at 13.2 an hour and 0 subscribers per 1,000. The script was not the problem: those who saw it watched 77.5% of it on average. Probable cause: Shorts on recent politics land below the usual here, and a book in the news did not change that. Test done: recent-politics Shorts stay off the list.

Each long-form view is getting shorter: views rose 18.0% week over week but watch time only 1.6%, and the 7-day average view is 27.3%. All three Ramayana long-forms lose most viewers in their first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing; 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged. Test: the Indonesia transcript in the scripts folder, so the check shows where its viewers left before the Bali script is written.

Shorts views fell 78.5% week over week to 2026-11-20: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November has left the window and nothing dated has gone up since. Search is no longer where most Shorts views come from (30.8% over 28 days). Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's search views over the coming weeks.

actions.action: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.
actions.rationale: Over the 365-day window it brings 34.2 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,081 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah) on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video.
actions.rationale: The script is written and cut, and it was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which has averaged 658 views an hour since it went up. That it sends viewers on is a guess.

actions.action: If not done yet, answer the two correction comments under the Indonesia long-form, the Majapahit one and the long fact-check, with sources (/replies drafts them).
actions.rationale: Both sit high on a video still bringing viewers, and the Bali script has to survive the same readers.

actions.action: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 19 views since 3 November.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.
actions.rationale: Search Console alone is thin: Google impressions for the site fell sharply from September to October, and every query that shows is the brand name.

growth.verdict: Needs 224 net subscribers a day. The channel does 59.81/day, so the target is a **3.7x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 59.8/day — still 3.7x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-08-22, 3.7 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1281 of the 3,131 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 28.7/day (804 of 1,555 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 39.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 142, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 446 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 28.7/day (804 of 1,555 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 28.7/day (804 of 1,555 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,281 subscribers on 73,074 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
